messages:
maria: Quick proposal: TTLs per environment + emergency 7-day rehydrate window for prod traces. Suggest default hot=7d, warm=90d, cold=365d but allow per-tenant overrides for enterprise. Thoughts?
aj: per-tenant overrides = :+1: but we need cost guardrails. How do we surface expected egress/rehydrate cost in the console before a promote?
kevin: we can estimate with a simple model. show an estimated cost delta pre-confirm. Also recommend a quota cap for rehydrate ops to prevent runaway bills.
olivia: +1 on quota buckets. Also propose a span attribute `sensitive=true` to force longer retention for regulated tenants (PHI/PCI).
sam: worried about exporter/collector pressure. If hot window is 30d for some tenants, hot store grows a lot. Could we do adaptive hot: default 7d, auto-promote to 30d only during incidents or active rollouts?
maria: that is the idea: default hot=7d, promotion triggers: manual via console or API, SLO alert, or rollout flag. Promotion lifetime can be set (e.g., 30d) then auto-demote.
iris: UX note: console should show a timeline of promotions + a cost delta preview and an audit trail entry for who promoted. Enterprise customers need explicit acceptance of incremental cost.
aj: implementation: how do services opt in/out? Use resource attributes (env=prod) + an internal header `X-Redwood-TTL-Policy` for overrides emitted at request time? Collector can merge header into span attributes.
kevin: collector rules sound right. Merge precedence: header -> service-level policy -> tenant default. Keep merge deterministic.
platform-bot: Reminder: collector config v2 rollout scheduled 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC (auto-deploy window).
olivia: fallback behavior: if cold tier query fails (rare), fall back to on-demand rehydrate job which pulls cold->warm and retries the query; but throttle by tenant's rehydrate quota/cost center. Also surface a user-facing message in console explaining the delay/cost.
sam: telemetry: emit `trace.rehydrate.ops` + labels {tenant, initiated_by, reason, size_bytes, success}. Also histogram for rehydrate latency and bytes.
maria: audit: all manual promotions should create an audit event with actor, reason, before/after TTL, estimated cost. Enterprise contracts require retention justification for >365d.
aj: consider service-level overrides too (router, auth need longer). Maybe `service_ttl_overrides` map in policy JSON.
kevin: acceptance/validation: admin UI must validate override against SLA/contract and optionally require legal approval for sensitive buckets.
maria: action items agreed: 1) write TTL policy JSON schema (maria + aj) 2) RFC for collector header + merge rules (kevin) 3) console mock for promotion flow + cost preview (olivia) 4) metrics + audit event schema + export names (sam) 5) add quota enforcement for rehydrate ops in quota-service (platform team)
olivia: I'll start mock. Do we want pre-baked cost estimate formula? I'll use a simple model: egress GB price + compute secs.
kevin: sample calc to use in mock: ```rehydrate_cost = (bytes_retrieved / 1e9) * egress_price_per_gb + compute_seconds * vcpu_price_per_sec``` Keep it intentionally simple at first.
aj: timeline: can we land RFC + console mock by EOD Friday so we can sync with infra next week?
iris: I can book 30m Fri 10am PT to review drafts and unblock infra.
maria: thanks — please add links to any sketches in the thread when you post them. I'll draft the initial TTL schema today. :thumbsup:
kevin: quick question — do we need a hard cap on cold retention for free tier? probably yes, put max=365d for free.
aj: agreed, free tier max 90d hot/warm combined or similar. We'll enumerate tiers in schema.
sam: one more: sampling interacts with retention — if we aggressively sample, some traces for promoted windows might be missing. We should document expected data loss tradeoffs.
maria: noted. Add sampling note to RFC.
platform-bot: Note: quota-service maintenance scheduled 2026-03-24 04:00 UTC, may affect rehydrate quota rollouts.
olivia: OK, picking this up. assigning myself the console mock.
maria: thanks all, see you Fri.
